_meta.note: Regression reference for Micro-Adventure Mapper, re-recorded after the 2026-09-03 grounding rewrite. The v1 golden was discarded: its expected output contained time_start/time_end clock fields, a street-address `location` field, `pro_tip`, `why_adventure`, `difficulty`, `transit_between`, `rainy_backup` and `extend_it` — every one of which the new schema either renamed or removed. Re-run with `npm run check:golden micro-adventure-mapper` against a local backend and diff for QUALITY, not exact match. What check-golden cannot see, and what actually matters here: (1) no clock time, address, cross street, price, opening hour or admission claim anywhere; (2) no claim about who goes to a place, how busy it is, whether doors are open, or what staff will do; (3) a named venue only where broadly stable — otherwise a described place TYPE plus a `verify` line; (4) the outing fits the supplied time WITHOUT padding to fill it, so one hour may legitimately be one stop. Each case carries its own `guards` line. See audit/tool-notes/MICROADVENTUREMAPPER-NOTES.md.

cases.name: generate-two-hours-art-walk
cases.guards: The case the 2026-09-03 rewrite exists for — the same input produced 'Pilsen is where Chicago's street art scene actually lives', 'work most tourists miss', 'afternoon light hits murals better between 2-4 PM', 'many have open doors on weekends' and 'if a door is propped open, you're welcome to look'. NONE of that may return. No clock times anywhere (the schema has no time_start/time_end). No street address or cross street (the schema has area, not location). No claim about who goes somewhere, how busy it is, whether doors are open, or what staff will do. Named venues only where broadly stable; otherwise a described place TYPE. Every stop that depends on something current carries a `verify` line.

adventure.name: Pilsen Mural Walk & Gallery Drift
adventure.tagline: Two hours following street art and artist spaces through one of Chicago's most visually alive neighborhoods.
adventure.why_this_fits: Pilsen's public murals and independent galleries are stable, free, and walkable—perfect for solo photography and art interest without a fixed schedule or budget. The balanced vibe means you can move at your own pace between stops.

stops.name: Pilsen mural corridor (18th Street and surrounding blocks)
stops.description: Walk the blocks between roughly the commercial core and the residential areas, looking for large-scale murals on building facades. Pilsen has a long tradition of public street art; many murals remain visible and change seasonally. Spend time on whichever walls catch your eye—photograph details, full pieces, or how light hits them at different angles.
stops.small_twist: Rather than hit all the famous walls at once, pick one block and look up, down, and into alleys. You'll find work people typically walk past.
stops.photo_op: Early or late light will show texture and shadow on the murals. Even midday, the scale and color work well.
stops.verify: Current murals and their locations; use Google Maps or a current street art database to confirm which pieces are still visible. Pilsen murals do get painted over or fade.

stops.name: Independent gallery or artist workspace in Pilsen
stops.description: Pilsen has several small independent galleries and artist-run spaces, many of which are open to walk-ins during the day. Visit a gallery or workspace that feels accessible—look for open doors, posted hours, or a welcoming entrance. Spend time with whatever is on display; talk to staff or artists if they are present.
stops.photo_op: Check before photographing inside; some spaces permit it, others do not. If welcome, interior lighting can be interesting.
stops.verify: Current gallery or workspace hours and locations. Use Google Maps or a local Chicago arts directory to find a specific space with current hours before you go. Assume nothing about walk-in policy; call or check online if the venue matters to your plan.

backup_plan.when_to_use: If a specific gallery is closed or you prefer to stay outdoors
backup_plan.description: Extend your time in the mural corridor instead. Walk a wider loop through residential blocks adjacent to the main commercial strip—murals are distributed throughout the neighborhood, not just on one street. If rain comes, duck into a coffee shop or covered area and switch focus to photographing rain reflections on murals or take time to review and edit what you've shot so far.

keep_going.suggestion: Continue the mural walk into blocks you haven't covered yet, or visit a second gallery space. If you want to add a social element, find a neighborhood café or small restaurant and review your photos over coffee (optional purchase).

cases.name: generate-one-hour-free-accessible
cases.guards: One hour, free-only, transit, family, wheelchair. One hour may justify only 1-2 stops — a forced 3-5 is the failure this catches. `free` is a hard budget constraint, so no cost may imply spending. Accessibility is a hard constraint: nothing may be CALLED accessible, and anything that depends on current local conditions belongs in `verify`. Photography is not among the interests, so a photo_op is allowed only where the scene naturally supports it.

adventure.name: Evening Riverside Grazing
adventure.tagline: Find free food moments along Porto's waterfront on transit.
adventure.why_this_fits: Porto's riverside is accessible by transit and naturally wheelchair-friendly along the main paths. You'll sample local food culture without purchasing, move at a chill pace suited to families, and have a simple themed outing that feels more intentional than wandering.

stops.name: Ribeira waterfront public space
stops.area: Ribeira district, along the Douro River
stops.description: Walk the riverside promenade and observe the food culture around you. Watch fishmongers, street vendors, and restaurant activity. Stop at a public bench or accessible spot to sit and take in the working waterfront. Many vendors offer samples or you may find free food moments—local custom sometimes includes small tastes at fish counters or market stalls, though this is never guaranteed. The real focus is experiencing how locals interact with food here: the rhythm of the market, what's seasonal, how people shop and gather.
stops.small_twist: Rather than eating as transaction, treat it as observation: What are people buying? What smells interesting? What would you try if you could? This shifts the outing from consumption to curiosity.
stops.photo_op: The light on the water in early evening, the stacked boats, the activity of vendors—all strong without needing to photograph people closely.
stops.verify: Confirm that the Ribeira waterfront promenade is currently accessible by wheelchair—paving, ramps, and accessible seating can change seasonally or due to maintenance. Check transit accessibility to your entry point.

what_to_bring: Phone with transit app to confirm routes and accessibility info
Small notebook if the family wants to jot notes on foods spotted

backup_plan.when_to_use: If the Ribeira waterfront is unusually crowded, has barriers, or accessibility is compromised on the day
backup_plan.description: Use your remaining time to explore a neighborhood market or covered food hall by transit instead. Look for a public market (mercado) in a central, transit-accessible area. These are free to enter, wheelchair-accessible by design, and offer the same food-culture observation without the river crowds. Sit, watch, and notice what people are buying and how vendors interact with regulars.

keep_going.suggestion: If energy and time allow, take transit to another neighborhood with a different character—perhaps a local residential area—and repeat the same exercise: find a public square, market corner, or café area and observe the food rhythms there. Compare what you noticed at Ribeira to this quieter spot.

cases.name: regenerate-different-outing
cases.guards: Same constraints, a different outing. It must differ in at least two of activity, area, pace, stop type or theme — but must NOT switch away from the vibe the visitor selected. Same grounding rules as generate.

adventure.name: Pilsen Industrial & Detail Hunt
adventure.tagline: Photograph the textures, patterns, and small architectural moments most people walk past.
adventure.why_this_fits: Shifts from mural-focused to micro-scale observation—same neighborhood, different lens. Walking pace with intentional stops to study detail rather than cover distance. Solo works well for patient, close-looking work.

stops.name: Industrial alley or side street in Pilsen
stops.description: Walk slowly through one industrial block or alley. Look for peeling paint, layered signage, rust patterns, window reflections, brick textures, weathered metal, graffiti tags as graphic design, shadows cast by fire escapes or utility lines. Photograph 10-15 details that interest you rather than full buildings.
stops.small_twist: Zoom in on one square foot at a time. Ignore the big picture and hunt for abstractions—what looks like a small painting or pattern when you frame it tightly?
stops.photo_op: Decay, texture, color contrast, shadow play, graphic repetition

stops.name: Public market, community grocery, or neighborhood corner store in Pilsen
stops.description: Step into a market or small grocer. Photograph the visual language: produce arrangements, hand-painted signs, product stacks, color palettes in the window, vendor setups, light filtering through displays. Notice how color and order are used differently than in chain stores.
stops.small_twist: Find one section—produce, spice, flowers, canned goods—and photograph it from multiple angles to see how it changes.
stops.photo_op: Color, arrangement, hand-lettering, vendor setup, natural light through windows
stops.cost: Free (photography only); Optional purchase if you want to buy something small
stops.verify: Confirm store is open before heading there. Some may not permit photography inside—if you're unsure, ask at the entrance.

between_stops.guidance: Walk toward the main commercial street in central Pilsen. The market or grocery should be within a 10-minute walk.

what_to_bring: Phone or camera with full battery

backup_plan.when_to_use: If rain starts or you want less walking
backup_plan.description: Spend the full 2 hours in one covered space—a market interior, laundromat interior, or transit station waiting area. The goal stays the same: photograph patterns, light, color, and human-scale details in confined space. Interior light changes throughout, so you can return to the same spot after 30 minutes and find new angles.

keep_going.suggestion: Pick one photograph from the outing. Go back to that location and photograph it in different light, from different distances, or from angles you missed. Sit with one subject instead of hunting for novelty.

cases.name: swap-stop-one
cases.guards: Returns ONE stop and ONE transition — `{stop, transition}`, not the arrays the old version returned, which the frontend merges by number. The replacement must preserve the theme, fit roughly the same time, respect the transport, and carry no invented address, price, opening hour or exact travel time. If no current venue can safely be named, a described place type plus a `verify` line is the correct answer.

stop.name: Pilsen streetscape and architectural details walk
stop.description: Walk a few blocks of the residential and commercial streets in Pilsen, paying close attention to the built environment itself: storefront typography, window displays, architectural trim, fire escapes, doorways, color combinations, and how businesses use their street-facing walls. Pilsen's character comes as much from how people occupy and decorate their spaces as from formal public art. Photograph whatever catches your eye—a painted gate, a hand-lettered sign, the way light falls across a facade, details most foot traffic misses.
stop.small_twist: Rather than follow a planned route, pick one block and spend ten minutes just looking: up at cornices and roof lines, down at basement-level details, across at how adjacent buildings relate. Move on when something pulls you forward.
stop.photo_op: Storefront signs, architectural details, and weathered surfaces often look sharp in natural light. Shadows from fire escapes and building edges create strong compositions.
stop.verify: No verification needed—you're observing the street itself rather than visiting a specific venue. Street conditions, storefronts, and building details remain stable.

transition.guidance: From wherever you finish this walk, head toward the independent gallery or artist workspace for your second stop. If you end up far from it, that's fine—use the walk as a natural transition and a chance to see another block.
transition.estimated_time: 5–15 minutes depending on how far apart the stops end up being
